title: Fennel and the Big Teal Lonely
subtitle: A story about feeling lonely
story: Fennel went to the park one day,
ready to swing and slide and play.
top
But Clover was gone to see her gran.
And everyone else had a friend or a plan.
top
Ducks played tag. Squirrels shared a ball.
Fennel stood still. He played with no one at all.
top
A big teal bubble rose up from the ground.
It wrapped him in quiet, without a sound.
top
Everything sounded far, far away.
He sat on a bench. He had nobody to play.
top
Mama came over. “Lonely is when
we’d love a friend, and we want one again.”
top
“First, LOOK around. Who is nearby?
Someone is there, with a kind little eye.”
top
“Next, say HELLO, with a smile that’s warm.
A hello can melt a lonely storm.”
top
“Last, INVITE. Ask someone to play.
‘Want to swing with me?’ That’s all you say.”
top
Fennel looked. A hedgehog, small and shy,
was drawing in the dirt with a stick nearby.
top
“Hello!” said Fennel. “Want to play?”
“Yes!” said Pip. “I hoped you’d say!”
top
The teal bubble floated away, soft as a sigh.
Look. Hello. Invite. And a friend is nearby.
top
note_lines: Stay close and listen before fixing.
Role-play a hello and an invitation at home.
Arrange short playdates and celebrate every try.

listing.description:
Fennel goes to the park, ready to swing and slide and play. But Clover is away, and everyone else already has a friend.

A big teal bubble rises up and wraps him in quiet. Everything sounds far away, until Mama Bear sits beside him and shows him how to find a friend.

With three friend steps — Look. Hello. Invite. — little readers learn that lonely is okay, and that a friend is nearby.

Inside this warm rhyming picture book:

  • A cozy read-aloud rhyme for ages 3–6, perfect for playgrounds and new schools
  • A kid-friendly image of loneliness as a quiet teal bubble that floats away
  • Three easy steps children can copy: Look, Hello, Invite
  • A note for grown-ups with simple ways to help a lonely child make friends
  • Soft watercolor-style illustrations

Book 9 in the Fennel's Feelings series. A gentle story about feeling alone and finding a friend.

Style: soft watercolor and gouache children's picture book, warm cozy palette, subtle paper texture. The setting is a sunny village park with swings, a slide, a pond with ducks and a big oak tree, with simple animal playmates (ducks, squirrels, rabbits). The 'loneliness' is a big, quiet, glass-like teal (blue-green) soap-bubble that rises around Fennel and mutes the world outside it, softly faded colors beyond the bubble (never a monster, no face). No text, letters or words anywhere in the image (no signs, labels or writing on anything).
